mira: Re: namespacing scheme. If we namespace runtime-added keys by (artifact_v, namespace, runtime_id), we can safely sweep when artifact_v increments. But that leaves a gap during partial rollouts where old and new artifact_v coexist.

ton y: That's the canary problem. We need a soft-sweep rule: keep keys for artifact_v and artifact_v-1 only. Anything older gets GC'd. Also require compiler to emit a compatibility hint that indicates whether a fast-swap is allowed.

alex: For partial rollouts we need to avoid node-id reassignments. Compiler should favor additive changes until the canary window closes. If a removal or rename is necessary, the compiler must produce a mapping table (old_node_id -> new_node_id) and mark it "transition":true so runtimes can migrate keys.

mira: Migration table idea is good. The compiler could also emit a "migration_ttl" to indicate how long runtimes should retain old keys for migration.

sam: ops-bot: policy-compiler 2.4 canary started (10%). Migration_ttl default=3600s will be applied.

ton y: We should also enforce a policy that node ids are namespaced by builder name to avoid collisions from parallel compilers. Eg: builder/142/zoneA/node123.

alex: Edge case: if migration table is large (>1k entries) it indicates a non-additive refactor; require a manual rollout plan. Compiler CI should fail in that case.

mira: Agreed. Add lint: migration-table length > 100 -> require arch-approval and manual rollout flag.

ops-bot: deploy-check: migration-table-size check applied in CI.

tony: One last note on soft-eval: runtime must attach a confidence score with each proof. Compiler checks confidence threshold before accepting advisory route. Default threshold 0.7.

alex: Nice. Anything else?

mira: I'll fold these into the RFC and add some diagrams for the lifecycle across canary windows.

alex: Thanks. We'll review RFC next Tuesday.
